reading.body:
Business interruption insurance for AI now spans ten distinct failure points, from utility load shedding and grid connection delays to hyperscaler outages and foundational API downtime.

The ten coverages map the physical and contractual dependencies of AI compute. Three concern electricity directly: utility load shedding and throttling, power purchase agreement failure, and interconnection queue delay. A fourth covers drought-related water shutoffs, which would halt cooling for data centers. This concentration reflects how grid access and power delivery have become operational risks, not just construction risks, for AI infrastructure.

The remaining coverages extend the same logic to network and software layers. Subsea fibre cuts and dark fibre backhaul disruption protect against severed connectivity, while GPU provider service level breaches, hyperscaler outage cascades, foundational API outages, and edge node update corruption cover failures in the compute and model supply chain. Together they treat an AI application as a chain of dependencies where any break triggers a claim.

What the data does not show is cost, frequency, or uptake. It lists ten product categories but no premiums, loss ratios, or evidence of how widely each is purchased. The presence of coverage indicates insurers see these as insurable risks, not that they are the most common or most expensive failures.
